hyperedges.label: DeltaTrim formula: Total Trim at stress idle minus Total Trim at low idle
Two-speed-idle gas transition matrix (low idle to 2500 RPM, GAS-* cases)
ECU hardware fault family routed by the proposed checker via Tables 1-3

hyperedges.description: Rich lambda_chem with positive trim is a truth-vs-perception contradiction indicating O2 bias or pre-sensor exhaust leak
Lean lambda_chem with negative trim is a truth-vs-perception contradiction indicating O2 silicone poisoning or wideband bias
abs(normalized_obd_lambda - lambda_chem) >= 0.08 emits perception_contradiction; gas chemistry wins on disagreement
composition.py writes downstream_trim_role onto OBDLivePayload; when CATALYST_MONITOR_ONLY, COMLab fault_atlas_router bypasses post-cat trim so P2096/P2099 cannot fire

o2_normalizer maps Ip to normalized_obd_lambda on WIDEBAND_LINEAR; persistent |lambda-1.0|>0.05 with healthy Ip slope raises WIDEBAND_OFFSET_CANDIDATE, which COMLab confirms against lambda_chem (O2-FU-1)
L3 correlation/discrepancy matrix computes Lambda_Delta_Vector = lambda_obd - lambda_chem inside COMLab perception_contradiction; significant delta exposes liar/blind/inversion scenarios

nodes.label: DELTA_TRIM
nodes.rationale: Primary diagnostic value of fuel trims (1990-2010 petrol) is the difference between trims at two engine speeds, not the value at one speed. Discriminating axis: whether trim improves or worsens under load. No live consumer yet; stays PENDING per SWEEP_MANIFEST FU-2 signal/noise rule.

nodes.label: TOTAL_TRIM
nodes.rationale: The engine evaluates total trim (STFT+LTFT), not STFT or LTFT in isolation, because LTFT can fully absorb a settled bias (e.g. vacuum leak as STFT 0% with LTFT +24%) and either value alone masks it.

nodes.label: LOW_IDLE
nodes.rationale: 600-800 RPM, zero external load (FuelTrimW); EcuSignatures uses 700-800 RPM. Maps to live RpmStateBucket.STABILIZED_IDLE (650-900).

nodes.label: STRESS_IDLE
nodes.rationale: Steady-state throttle hold 3500-4500 RPM, park/neutral (FuelTrimW + EcuSignatures). Band conflict: Vol7 gas-side uses 2500 RPM; reconcile in FU-2 / O2-FU-3 before fusing OBD and gas sides.

nodes.label: VACUUM_LEAK
nodes.rationale: High manifold vacuum at low idle (18-22 in-Hg) pulls unmetered air downstream of MAF; leak is large fraction of low idle airflow (lean, +15..+25% trim) but negligible at 3500-4500 RPM, so trims normalise and DeltaTrim goes <= -10%. Signature only valid on MAF closed-loop architecture.

nodes.label: FUEL_STARVATION
nodes.rationale: Weak pump/clogged filter/leaking FPR holds rail pressure at minimal idle demand (trims ~0..+5%) but cannot meet 3500-4500 RPM fuel demand, dropping rail pressure -> lean -> trims +15..+25%, DeltaTrim >= +10%.

nodes.label: MAF_UNDERREPORT
nodes.rationale: Contamination insulates the MAF hot-wire; error minimal at low idle but at high airflow the wire fails to register high-velocity cooling and under-reports air mass -> ECU underfuels -> lean -> DeltaTrim >= +10%. Separated from fuel starvation by low-idle band (tolerates up to +8%) and MAF g/s plausibility.

nodes.label: EXHAUST_BACKPRESSURE
nodes.rationale: Clogged cat/crushed pipe vents fine at low exhaust volume (trims ~0%) but at 3500-4500 RPM backpressure traps inert gas, cutting volumetric efficiency -> locally rich -> trims <= -12%, DeltaTrim <= -10%. Delta-only signature; no row in the static decision tree. Separated from vacuum leak by stress-idle trim sign.

nodes.label: COMLab delta-calculation script
nodes.rationale: Proposed consumer (SWEEP_MANIFEST FU-2) for all DeltaTrim chunks. Per signal/noise rule every delta field stays PENDING until this script reads it in a live code path. Must branch on air-metering architecture (MAF vs speed-density, forced induction) before applying profiles 02-05.

nodes.label: SPEED_DENSITY
nodes.rationale: Speed-Density paradox: on a MAP-only engine leak air raises MAP, the ECU references a higher VE cell and adds matching fuel, IAC closes to hold RPM -> trims stay near 0%, DeltaTrim ~ 0 for a real leak. Leak shows instead as reduced IAC counts, elevated idle MAP (~45 vs ~30 kPa), idle flare.

nodes.label: TURBO_BOOST_LEAK
nodes.rationale: Under boost a post-turbo leak lets already-metered air escape: MAF counted it but it never reached the cylinders -> rich -> trims up to ~-20% STFT, the exact opposite of a naturally-aspirated vacuum leak. Delta script must know forced-induction state before a positive-trim leak verdict.

nodes.label: DELTA_GAS
nodes.rationale: Diagnostic value of a 5-gas reading is the change from curb idle to stabilised 2500 RPM. Vacuum-dependent faults attenuate at 2500 RPM; speed-dependent mechanical faults intensify. Only the sign of Delta-gas across the speed step separates faults reading identically at idle (e.g. GAS-WVS improves vs GAS-WPR worsens). GASLab owns per-state frames (stateless); COMLab owns cross-state delta math.

nodes.label: GAS-VAC-001
nodes.rationale: Vacuum-line FPR rupture: rich attenuates at 2500 RPM - lower vacuum cuts leak flow + dilution.

nodes.label: GAS-LEAN-001
nodes.rationale: Intake vacuum leak: lean attenuates at 2500 RPM - leak negligible vs metered air.

nodes.label: GAS-EAL-001
nodes.rationale: Pre-cat exhaust leak: positive exhaust pressure at 2500 RPM blocks air ingress; false-rich trim corrects.

nodes.label: GAS-WPR-001
nodes.rationale: Worn piston rings: oil burn intensifies at 2500 RPM (blow-by + ring speed).

nodes.label: GAS-WVS-001
nodes.rationale: Worn valve seals: oil induction clears at 2500 RPM - vacuum drop stops guide pull.

nodes.label: GAS-FC-001
nodes.rationale: Flat camshaft lobe: restricted lift = high-speed breathing misfire at 2500 RPM.

nodes.label: GAS-ESC-001
nodes.rationale: EGR stuck closed: no dilution -> NOx runaway past 1370 C (1500 -> 2800 ppm).

nodes.label: GAS-ESO-001
nodes.rationale: EGR stuck open: high intake volume at 2500 RPM dilutes stuck EGR; stabilises.

nodes.label: GAS-EVAP-001
nodes.rationale: Saturated EVAP: purge opens at 2500 RPM -> raw-vapour spike (worsens).

nodes.label: GAS-CNL-001
nodes.rationale: Cold cat (no light-off): thermal light-off at 2500 RPM - healthy cat recovers.

nodes.label: GAS-COV-001
nodes.rationale: Cat overload/blow-through: residence time too short - gases blow through at both speeds.

nodes.label: GASLab
nodes.rationale: Owning lab for the per-state 5-gas frame; stays stateless per isolation contract - cross-state delta math belongs to COMLab.

nodes.label: COMLab delta engine
nodes.rationale: Same proposed FU-2 consumer that reads DeltaTrim; gas-side name used in Vol7 chunks. Must skip delta computation on frames failing the vsum validity gate.

nodes.label: VSUM
nodes.rationale: vsum = HC+CO+CO2+O2+NOx (% volume). Valid 14.0-18.0%; <14% severe dilution (probe/tailpipe leak); >18% near-ambient/exhaust leak bypassing cat. Diluted samples produce false-lean lambda and corrupt every downstream delta, so the gate must run before any Delta-gas or Brettschneider-lambda. The vsum display equation was image-stripped in Vol7 export; thresholds survive in prose.

nodes.label: GAS_SAMPLE_VALID
nodes.rationale: Per-frame validity flag GASLab marks alongside vsum; field + consumer (COMLab delta engine skip) ship together per v2 forward-progress rule. A frame failing vsum at idle but passing at 2500 RPM is itself a sampling-integrity signature, not an engine fault.

nodes.label: DILUTION_FAIL
nodes.rationale: CO + CO2 <= 6.0%: too much ambient air for a reliable profile.

nodes.label: delta-relations
nodes.rationale: Whole-folder status STAGING: every chunk consumer PENDING (FU-2). Preserves formulas + magnitudes so the delta script spec can be written against ground truth; nothing ships into the engine until a live code path reads DeltaTrim. Complementary to fuel-trim/04 static pattern table, not duplicate.

nodes.label: LOAD_PCT
nodes.rationale: J1979 calculated load. Field is live (ingested as a PID); the closed-form WOT formula is provenance only - no live evaluator, and it references AAT which has no OBDLivePayload field.

nodes.label: perception_contradiction.detect
nodes.rationale: Live consumer of the truth-vs-perception principle: ECU hardware faults are isolated by divergence between OBD perception (lambda_obd) and 5-gas ground truth (lambda_chem). Its Lambda Truth guard suppresses sensor-bias verdicts when lambda_chem < 0.90 or > 1.10 - by design, so deeply abnormal ECU-hardware chemistry (0.72-1.55) falls outside the bias path and needs the proposed dedicated checker instead.

nodes.label: RpmStateBucket.STABILIZED_IDLE
nodes.rationale: Live bucket 650-900 RPM; covers the doc's low-idle band 700-800.

nodes.label: RpmStateBucket.STRESS_IDLE
nodes.rationale: Live bucket 3000-4500 RPM; matches FuelTrimW/EcuSignatures 3500-4500 stress band. O2logic.md uses 2500 RPM - keep ECU deltas on 3500-4500 per O2-FU-3.

nodes.label: ECU_HARDWARE_FAULT
nodes.rationale: Fault class v1 cannot detect: internal ECU component decay corrupts the closed-loop control loop so the OBD datastream lies while exhaust chemistry does not.

nodes.label: ECU_CAPACITOR_LEAK
nodes.rationale: Leaked electrolyte dissolves PCB traces -> high-impedance paths + AC ripple on DC reference lines. Signature is rhythmic instability, not a fixed offset: symmetric +/-15% STFT oscillation both banks + erratic LOAD_PCT at low idle, collapsing to frozen 0% trims + open loop at stress idle. B1~B2 symmetry is the tell vs single-bank sensor fault, but no live path reads B1-vs-B2 divergence today.

nodes.label: ECU_HARDWARE_CHECKER
nodes.rationale: Proposed COMLab/OBDLab ECU-hardware-fault checker (proposals/OBD_ImplProp.md, ECU-FU-1) - the named consumer for all five proposed ECU fault modes. Registered as proposal, not deferral, per the v2 forward-progress rule: a dedicated checker (not a tweak to the bias detector) is right because the Lambda Truth guard deliberately suppresses on these modes' abnormal chemistry. Loads the Tables 1-3 discriminator matrix; drives companion proposals ECU-FU-2 (B1-vs-B2 divergence reader) and ECU-FU-3 (TPS/IAT fields).

nodes.label: INJECTOR_DRIVER_OPEN
nodes.rationale: Open-circuit low-side driver: one cylinder dead on B1 pumps pure air -> upstream O2 pegs lean, STFT/LTFT B1 pinned +25%, B2 balanced, held across both idle bands. Surviving B1 cylinders run rich from global max enrichment (deceptive CO alongside high O2).

nodes.label: INJECTOR_DRIVER_SHORT
nodes.rationale: Drain-source fuse -> injector sprays constantly -> flooded cylinder, rich misfire; B1 trims pinned -25%, lambda_chem 0.78-0.81. Overlaps detect_compensated_rich's railed-negative-trim pattern but its lambda_chem is outside that detector's stoich window [0.95,1.05], so the live detector would not fire - and would mis-verdict 'fuel leak' if it did. Bank asymmetry is the signal, unread today.

nodes.label: COIL_DRIVER_SHORT
nodes.rationale: Thermal short -> 100% duty -> coil melts open -> permanent single-cylinder ignition misfire on B1. Deceptive-lambda trap: dead cylinder pumps raw fuel AND air in stoich proportion so lambda_chem stays ~1.01 while HC ~2200 ppm - lambda alone hides the misfire; HC + O2 expose it. No PID uniquely separates internal driver from external plug/coil/wire, which is why this stays a proposal.

nodes.label: CATALYST_OVERWHELMED
nodes.rationale: Raw HC + O2 ignite in the catalyst at stress idle -> substrate > 900 C (melt risk).

nodes.label: ChemicalSignature.IGNITION_MISFIRE
nodes.rationale: Live GASLab classification of the exhaust symptom only - does not localise to the ECU coil driver; that is the proposed checker's job.

nodes.label: SENSOR_GROUND_TRACE_OPEN
nodes.rationale: Vaporised internal reference-ground trace floats sensor ground to 1.5-4.5 V, corrupting every ratiometric sensor at once: ECT/IAT locked -40 C, TPS 100%, LOAD_PCT 80-100% on a parked warmed engine, frozen trims, severe rich (lambda_chem ~0.72). All-banks symmetric locked-sensor pattern is the strongest internal-ECU tell vs single external sensor fault. Blocking gap: TPS and IAT have no OBDLivePayload fields (ECU-FU-3).

nodes.label: ECT
nodes.rationale: Maps to live coolant_temp_c (range -40..140).

nodes.label: IAT
nodes.rationale: No live OBDLivePayload field; companion proposal ECU-FU-3 - field only added if the proposed checker names it as consumer.

nodes.label: TPS
nodes.rationale: No live OBDLivePayload field; companion proposal ECU-FU-3 - field only added if the proposed checker names it as consumer.

nodes.label: VREF_RAIL_COLLAPSE
nodes.rationale: Internal 5V regulator drifts down (e.g. 4.1 V); MCU still scales against 5.0 V so every ratiometric reading is suppressed -> false lean fuel-starve. Mirror image of mode 4 (there sensors floated high/false rich). Discriminator: symmetric +25% both banks + severely lean tailpipe (high O2/NOx) + flat-low ratiometric voltages + LOAD_PCT that won't scale with RPM. Pinned-positive trim that cannot lean a genuinely-lean tailpipe points at the rail, not a sensor. NOT the fuel-pressure regulator.

nodes.label: HIGH_COMBUSTION_TEMP
nodes.rationale: Ultra-lean + high speed -> combustion-temp spike -> NOx ~350 ppm, anomalous in neutral.

nodes.label: total_trim_correction_delta_b2
nodes.rationale: Emitted by OBDLab but read nowhere in comlab non-test code - the symmetric/asymmetric bank discriminator (strongest internal-vs-external tell) has no consumer. ECU-FU-2 closes this orphan: add the consumer, do not add a field.

nodes.label: bank_symmetry
nodes.rationale: External sensor/harness faults are typically bank-specific; internal faults touching a shared plane (reference ground, VREF) hit both banks symmetrically. B1-vs-B2 symmetry is a primary discriminator.

nodes.label: deceptive_lambda
nodes.rationale: Single-cylinder coil/injector faults pump raw fuel + raw O2 in stoich proportion, so lambda_chem ~1.01 looks normal while HC ~2200 ppm screams misfire. Never clear a fault on lambda alone - read HC and O2.

nodes.label: Comparative Signature Tables (Tables 1-3)
nodes.rationale: Reference matrix for all five ECU modes (tailpipe emissions + lambda; live OBD PID signatures; O2 sensor configuration behaviour). Preserved verbatim as the proposed checker's discriminator input - the analogue of fault_atlas_router's discriminator table. Live-field gaps: TPS and IAT columns have no payload fields.

nodes.label: TrimAnalyticsGate.STARTUP_T15_ACTIVE
nodes.rationale: Proposed gate: T15 init clears transient KAM and lambda runs open-loop off lookup maps until closed loop is reached, so trims/lambda in the key-on window are transient and must not be routed as faults. Numeric rich/lean limits PENDING readable export (Vol2 MD12 cells image-stripped).

nodes.label: TrimAnalyticsGate.HIGH_LOAD_ENRICH_ACTIVE
nodes.rationale: >=70% calculated load: PCM goes open-loop, ignores O2 feedback to protect the engine, inhibits EVAP purge, pulls timing - normal enrichment would otherwise read as a rich fault. Pressure-delta faults (P0087) and MAF peak-resolution issues surface above 70% load.

nodes.label: control_module_voltage_v
nodes.rationale: Scalar OBDLab emission of VPWR (PID 0x42), no verdict. Field + consumer ship together as proposal EP-OBD-IN-04.

nodes.label: VPWR
nodes.rationale: Supply voltage at PCM pins; every sensor reference is built on a clean DC rail, so a low/high/ripply rail shifts stoichiometric points and sensor references before any air/fuel sensor is at fault. Must be ruled out first or the engine blames the wrong subsystem. Healthy ~13.5-14.7 V running; <12.0 V charging/ground fault; >15.0 V over-charging/AC ripple.

nodes.label: DELTA_VPWR
nodes.rationale: Low-to-high idle sweep: DeltaVPWR < -1.0 V under revs = alternator/regulator diode fault; > +2.5 V (system > 15.5 V) = over-charging, ripple into sensor references -> EP-FA-05. AC ripple is inferred downstream from DeltaVPWR - VPWR is a scalar read, not a waveform.

nodes.label: COMLab electrical-health pre-check
nodes.rationale: Proposed perception_contradiction.py pre-check (T-COMV2-VPWR-GATE-1): down-weights/suppresses sensor-fault candidates when the PCM rail is out of band so a charging fault is not mis-routed as an O2/MAF fault.

nodes.label: EP-FA-05
nodes.rationale: Alternator-AC-ripple fault node; charging-side faults route here.

nodes.label: ecu-diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Folder delivers five forward-progress fault PROPOSALS + one active method chunk, per the v2-rework rule: internal ECU hardware failures are precisely what v1 cannot detect and v2 exists to fix, so they ship as proposals with a nameable consumer (ECU-FU-1 checker), not deferrals. They refine existing ecu_fault.json nodes (ERR-EF-006, ERR-EF-007, ERR-ECU-001), not duplicate them.

nodes.label: COMLab trim analytics
nodes.rationale: ACTIVE consumer: total-trim symptom generation feeding fault-atlas Air-and-Fuel-Metering routing (P0171/P0172/P0174/P0175).

nodes.label: POSITIVE_TRIM
nodes.rationale: System running lean; ECU adding fuel. Universal across OBD-II per SAE J1979 PID $06/$07.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE_TRIM
nodes.rationale: System running rich; ECU subtracting fuel.

nodes.label: trim_sign
nodes.rationale: The sign is the comparison key for truth-vs-perception fusion against gas-chemistry lambda.

nodes.label: trim_sign_uncertain
nodes.rationale: Raised for <=1995 vehicles: some Asian-market pre-OBD-II proprietary ECUs use the opposite sign convention, so the truth-vs-perception comparison must not assume the standard table.

nodes.norm_label: p01xx/p02xx air & fuel metering, thermal, injector circuits

nodes.norm_label: p03xx ignition & misfire and the misfire-vs-fuelling trim discriminator

nodes.norm_label: p04xx/p05xx/p06xx egr, evap, catalyst, idle control, control modules

nodes.norm_label: ltft load-cell matrix (maf x rpm) proposal

nodes.norm_label: dtc enable-criteria envelope and blocking codes

nodes.norm_label: pcm memory, freeze-frame and repair verification

nodes.label: Bias vs real mixture - the truth-vs-perception rule
nodes.norm_label: bias vs real mixture - the truth-vs-perception rule

nodes.label: SUPPRESS_POST_CAT_TRIM
nodes.rationale: Declined as a TrimAnalyticsGate value: post-cat suppression already carried by downstream_trim_role = CATALYST_MONITOR_ONLY; a second gate value would be duplicate signal. Doc bug O2-FU-2 — source O2logic.md/SWEEP_MANIFEST §11 assert a non-existent enum member.

nodes.label: downstream_trim_role
nodes.rationale: Carrier of post-cat trim suppression on the OBDLivePayload typed JSON boundary; chosen over a gate value because the gate governs whether all trim analytics run, not routing-out of post-cat trim.

nodes.label: WIDEBAND_OFFSET_CANDIDATE
nodes.rationale: v2 addition (O2-FU-1, two-stage): emitted by o2_normalizer when sensor=WIDEBAND_LINEAR and persistent |normalized_obd_lambda - 1.0| > 0.05 with healthy Ip slope; COMLab confirms against lambda_chem. Promoted from source-doc term BIASED_OFFSET with a named consumer rather than deferred.

nodes.label: BIASED_OFFSET
nodes.rationale: Source-doc term accepted as v2 addition: promoted to the two-stage WIDEBAND_OFFSET expression (O2-FU-1) with named consumer, not withheld for being absent from v1.

nodes.label: inferred_baro_delta
nodes.rationale: Catches a MAF that is out of calibration and corrupting fuel control while setting no DTC (L3 blindness class) — computed BARO at hard WOT vs local actual.

nodes.label: MAF-MAP-TPS rationality
nodes.rationale: Cross-checks the three load sensors so a single drifted air sensor cannot corrupt the whole fuel strategy — one liar is caught by the other two.

nodes.label: fault_atlas ignition family
nodes.rationale: PROPOSAL consumer for manual-entry waveform features (firing_kv, burn_ms, ripple_count) — no live OBD stream supplies these, so per signal/noise the consumer must be specced before any field ships.

nodes.label: secondary-ignition-waveform
nodes.rationale: Resolves what the misfire monitor cannot: ignition failure vs lean mixture vs low compression — burn-time and ripple count separate a lean mixture from a worn plug, both of which raise the firing line.

nodes.label: fault_atlas GDI fuel branch
nodes.rationale: PROPOSAL consumer — desired-vs-actual rail pressure + VCV duty isolate HPFP/lift-pump faults (P0087/P0088) that trim logic alone mis-attributes. Fields earn their place via this named consumer only.

nodes.label: internal pump leak / weak lift pump
nodes.norm_label: internal pump leak / weak lift pump

nodes.label: w_theo
nodes.rationale: Speed-density theoretical airflow W_theo = (eta_V * V_disp * P_manifold * RPM) / (120 * R * T_intake) — reference against which MAF non-linearity is measured.

nodes.label: sensor_error_delta
nodes.rationale: Two-point non-linearity delta (2500 vs 750 RPM error vs W_theo). Threshold ladder: <3-4% healthy; 5-12% calibration drift/dirty MAF (DTC-silent); >12-15% component fault, typically sets P0101. A single snapshot misses a contaminated hot-wire MAF that reads plausibly at idle but under-reports under load.

nodes.label: monitor_readiness
nodes.rationale: A monitor that has not completed reports no fault because it never looked, not because the system is healthy. Encoding 'no DTC => component OK' without this qualifier is the single most dangerous false-truth the engine can ingest. Manual-entry field; ships only together with the analytics_preconditions reader (signal/noise).

nodes.label: DTC state machine and confidence weighting (pids-protocol/08)
nodes.norm_label: dtc state machine and confidence weighting (pids-protocol/08)

nodes.label: FMEM
nodes.rationale: Failure mode effects management: on a sensor fault the PCM substitutes a safe default value so the car can limp home. A scan tool then reports that default, which looks like a real reading but is a fabricated constant — ingesting it as a measurement produces confident, wrong inferences.

nodes.label: dtc_state
nodes.rationale: A DTC is not a boolean: the same P-code carries different evidential weight by lifecycle state. Fault-atlas must weight states differently or it chases ghosts (pending one-offs) and trusts false all-clears (MIL-off history codes read as fixed).

nodes.label: pids-protocol
nodes.rationale: Every chunk in this pack is a PROPOSAL: each names a producer + reader, but none of the PID streams/feature sets is yet an input field. Per signal/noise, fields ship only when the named consumer is specced and reads them.

nodes.label: Euro tier
nodes.rationale: DNALab resolves the Euro tier from VIN/year; fault_atlas uses it to enable/disable family branches — prevents proposing an era-impossible fault (e.g. GPF-clog only Era 3, distributor PIP only Era 1).

nodes.label: era-make-priors
nodes.rationale: A prior-probability layer weighting candidates by the vehicle's era + manufacturer known-failure patterns (e.g. Ford FPDM corrosion, Chrysler TIPM relay, BMW HPFP) over the standards-based J2012 routing.

nodes.label: L3
nodes.rationale: L3 Correlation & Discrepancy Matrix is the truth-vs-perception junction — already implemented as the lambda_obd/lambda_chem override (COMLab perception_contradiction). Engine treats sensor data as mediated perception, not objective truth; gas chemistry arbitrates.

nodes.label: L5
nodes.rationale: L5 decision fusion & prognosis is the part v2 does not yet have — its proposed fields (Perception_Reliability_Index, ECU_Consistency_Score, Thermal_State_Confidence) are PROPOSAL, named with a consumer per forward-progress rules.

nodes.label: Lambda_Delta_Vector
nodes.rationale: Signed float lambda_obd - lambda_chem: 0 = perfect calibration; >0 engine physically leaner than ECU perceives (Rich-Blind ECU); <0 physically richer (Lean-Blind ECU). Quantifies the liar/blind delta for the L3 matrix.

nodes.label: Thermal_State_Confidence
nodes.rationale: Boolean: catalyst above light-off? If false, L3 discrepancies are treated as expected transient, not faults.

nodes.label: diagnostic_blindness
nodes.rationale: A sensor failing inside the ECU's plausible window (e.g. MAF under-reporting 15%) sets no DTC but shifts lambda — gas truth is the sanity check.

nodes.label: logic_inversion
nodes.rationale: Exhaust leaks / misfires make the ECU add fuel ('I'm lean') which drives the real state rich; caught at L3 via negative correlation between trim movement and lambda_chem improvement.

nodes.label: systemic_masking
nodes.rationale: Efficient catalysts hide engine misbehaviour until catastrophic failure; needs a pre-cat inference model (inlet/outlet temp differential).

nodes.label: Chemical_Efficiency_Score
nodes.rationale: CO2/(CO2+CO) — fraction of carbon fully oxidised; near 1.0 (>~0.95) healthy, low = fundamental combustion failure. Exact form prose-derived (standard combustion-efficiency ratio), flagged in formula wiki.

nodes.label: Oxygen_Usage_Factor
nodes.rationale: O2/CO (qualitative): high O2 with high CO/HC = misfire (both reactants pass unburned, combustion never happened); high CO with near-zero O2 = pure rich over-fuelling. Resolves the apparent 'simultaneously rich and lean' reading.

nodes.label: truth-perception
nodes.rationale: New pack from the Vol1 volume sweep: extends o2-logic/05 (O2-only view) to the full 5-tier engine framing with lambda_chem as ground truth.
